monument_type: Shrine, Mobile, Tiered temple, Archaeological object(s)
description_en: Temple of the goddess Kālikā and medieval statues.The monument is located on a small hill, south of the Dullu palace (now destroyed). Adjacent to it is the temple of Bhairava (DLK0350).The temple is oriented to the south-east. It is built in bricks and covered by a two-storied tile roof. It has a single room, accessed through a door in the south-east wall. Inside the sanctum, a small stepped platform is built along the north-western wall. Various objects of devotion and offerings are deposited on it. Among the objects is a stone statue of a seated deity (001), possibly Avalokiteśvara or Maitreya. This statue is installed inside the temple. Other statues include a broken Buddha (002), a broken Jina (003). The latter sculptures are placed inside a hypaethral concrete shrine of Kālikā built directly north-east of the temple. At the centre of the shrine's altar is an eroded sculpture of an unidentified seated deity (004), worshipped as an image of Kālikā. The Buddhist and Jain statues may be dated from the 10th to the 14th century, a period corresponding to the Yatse kingdom being under the sway of the Guge-Purang kings (10th–12th century) and of their 'Khaśa Malla’ successors (12th-14th century).The first roof is supported by wooden pillars installed all around the sanctum. The floor of the temple and the platform on which it stands has been cemented.The temple is dedicated to the goddess Kālika. She is thekuldevatāof Bhandari Chetris, the ancient treasurers of the Dullu kings (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009).Architectural elements are placed in different locations in and around the the temple. They broadly date from the medieval period. The actual monument may have been built in the 19th century, or during the 20th century.A building of the Nepal Police was recently built in the western side of the hill. The presence of this office leads to a lot of coming and going and the parking of vehicles between the Kālikā and the Bhairava temples. A ping pong table made of cement was built 2 meters west of the Bhairava Temple.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: REFERENCES Lecomte-Tilouine, Marie. 2009. Bards and Mediums . DVD. Almora: Almora Book Depot.
